answers: A hacker going by The Dark Overlord claims to have stolen and released 10 episodes of the new season of Orange Is the New Black more than a month before its official release on Netflix. Variety reports the hacker was demanding an unspecified ransom from Netflix, uploading the first episode of the upcoming fifth season to a file-sharing site Friday as proof. The next nine episodes were uploaded early Saturday morning after The Dark Overlord claims Netflix refused to pay them. The hacker says they're "quite ashamed to breathe the same air" as Netflix, as they were being entirely "reasonable and merciful" with their ransom offer. Neither Variety nor the AP have been able to—legally—confirm the authenticity of the episodes uploaded by The Dark Overlord. The new Orange Is the New Black episodes were apparently stolen months ago. Netflix says a production vendor "had its security compromised"; Variety identifies that vendor as Larson Studios, a post-production facility. The Dark Overlord says they weren't able to steal the final three episodes of the season because they weren't finished yet. The Dark Overlord told the AP in February they wouldn't release any of the stolen episodes; it's unclear why that changed. The hacker also claims to have stolen TV series from ABC, National Geographic, Fox, and IFC via the hack at Larson Studios. They're reportedly seeking a "modest" ransom for those as well. The leak of new Orange is the New Black episodes could hurt Neflix's subscriber numbers and stock price. The FBI is investigating.

full.prediction:
**Summary of News:**

A hacker known as "The Dark Overlord" has claimed to have stolen and released the first 10 episodes of the upcoming fifth season of Netflix's popular series *Orange Is the New Black* (OITNB) online, following an alleged extortion attempt that went unanswered by Netflix. The episodes were reportedly uploaded to the Pirate Bay, though their authenticity has not been independently verified. The hacker also claimed to have stolen unreleased content from other networks, including ABC, Fox, National Geographic, and IFC, as a result of a cyberattack on Larson Studios in late 2016.

Netflix had originally planned to release season five on June 9, but the leak may force the streaming service to consider moving up the premiere date. The hacker, in a public message, expressed frustration with Netflix, accusing the company of failing to meet their demands and warning that the company would suffer significant financial losses. The hacker also extended a "modest" ransom offer to other networks, urging them to pay to prevent further leaks.

Netflix confirmed that a production vendor used by multiple TV studios had been breached, and the FBI and other authorities are investigating the incident. The company has not yet commented on the specific impact of the leak on its business, but the incident could affect subscriber growth and stock performance. *Orange Is the New Black* is one of Netflix's most-watched original series, and the show has been renewed for seasons 5, 6, and 7, with creator Jenji Kohan set to continue as showrunner.

This incident is part of a broader trend of cyberattacks targeting Hollywood studios and streaming services, with rumors of large-scale leaks circulating online. While the authenticity of the stolen content remains unconfirmed, the potential for financial and reputational damage to Netflix is significant. The situation highlights the growing threat of cybercrime in the entertainment industry and the challenges faced by streaming platforms in protecting their intellectual property.
